D018_l001.question:
A 28-year-old single female public defender presents with a 4-month history of trauma-related symptoms following exposure to a traumatic event in the course of her work. She reports marked physiological arousal (e.g., palpitations, sweating, shortness of breath) when confronted with internal or external cues that resemble aspects of the trauma. The patient makes sustained efforts to avoid external reminders, including certain clients, case types, locations, and discussions associated with the event.

She describes persistent negative beliefs about others, including a generalized view that people are dangerous and untrustworthy. There is ongoing, pervasive guilt and self-blame regarding her perceived role in the traumatic circumstances.

Arousal and reactivity symptoms include difficulty initiating sleep, with prolonged sleep latency most nights, as well as episodes of intense verbal outbursts toward colleagues and close contacts characterized by shouting and blaming. She also reports engaging in reckless behaviors, such as driving at excessive speeds, with limited regard for personal safety.

These symptoms have been present for 4 months, are temporally linked to the identified traumatic stressor, and have resulted in significant impairment in occupational functioning, interpersonal relationships, and overall quality of life.
D018_l001.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
